lines.text: The axebeak gets dragged over. It's towering above you—more than twice your height. The handler looks down and says, "Can you even get on that thing?" There aren't really stands, just crowds gathered around. You're about halfway through the races, and a few people have managed to get pretty far. There's a large collection of rocks about ten feet from the starting line. It seems many people don't get particularly far.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: With a seven-foot animal, you might get thrown forward immediately. Even one step, you know.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So,

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I've got some goat meat. I'm not going to try to stick its bill together, because I don't think it would enjoy that. And I think other people can heal me, so I'm going to start by using Animal Handling and the food to persuade this thing to sit down so I can climb onto it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Many candidates.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: He doesn't have dates. He just has goat meat. Make an Animal Handling check. It looks at you and pauses. It leans into the rope and bends a little, but doesn't get all the way down to the ground. It's clearly about to run off, and the handler, holding on, says, "It's now or never."

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: All right. I'll climb the fence next to it and, from the fence, hop onto its back.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: That

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Eating at me.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Yeah, I'll hold a little bit of goat up to it to start with.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay, make a Dex check. You get on board and hold on with one hand as the animal starts bucking—

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: And

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: You know,

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: —and bouncing underneath you. It starts to move. You reach up, trying to get your hand to its beak to feed it the meat, and it lunges and takes a giant bite out of your hand. Four points of damage.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Manager.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It takes off down the course. Make an Animal Handling check, but use Dex instead of Wisdom, so add an extra plus one, I believe.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: What's the crowd reaction at this point.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: There's a gasp from the crowd. As you're bleeding, you look over and see Callie Charmheart saying, "Oh no."

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Oh, man. It takes a bite out of my hand, and I don't even flinch. I'm focused. I don't want to spook this thing. All right, here we go again.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It comes

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: With the additional plus one, should I get advantage because I'm smaller than most of the riders, so it's easier for me?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You would, except you rolled so badly on your Dex check that you would normally have disadvantage. That's countered by the advantage for being small.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Excellent. All right, here it comes. Sorry.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Twenty-one. You don't make it the farthest, but you pass almost all the stones. You're hanging on with blood dripping off your hand, and your small size is definitely helping. The way it runs is very different from a horse because it has only two legs, so there's this terrific ka-dunk, ka-dunk, and every step jolts you. After about sixty-five feet, you start to slide off. You wrap your arms around it and get another fifteen feet before landing on the ground about eighty feet down. You can see only one stone ahead of you.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: All right, all right, I'll take it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The crowd acknowledges you. You didn't start particularly well, but you made it in the end. Okay, Kenzo, what's your strategy?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: After getting myself into a deeply meditative state, I eliminate my own ego. When I approach the animal, it won't sense my human nature—only an incredibly peaceful and calming energy. I've eliminated any agitation and am emanating a deep sense of calm and centeredness. When I approach my axebeak, I'm basically trying to—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh, can I

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Can I—oh, I guess, what does that other thing I can do? Am I going to do a new thing now? Right, it's just sensing whether it's nervous or something.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Ah, yep, yep. Let me just check one thing

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay, influence anything. I can just see if it's—you can't influence anything?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No, it's not smart enough to—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: —to have any. Got it. That's fine. I approach with a tremendously deep sense of calm. I thought this was also going to be Acrobatics in addition to Animal Handling.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Is that true

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Ah, it depends on what you do.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: After getting into this deep state of calm, I was going to use Animal Handling to keep it calm, then use all my acrobatic skills to stay on the thing as long as I can.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Staying on the thing is Animal Handling, but you use Dexterity instead of Wisdom. For you, that would be—

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Not perfect. Sixteen.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I am. I've got plus three and one

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It would be plus three—a straight Animal Handling check.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: If you want to try anything tricky, that might involve other rolls.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I want to do the tricky thing that will give me my plus-five Acrobatics. I want to make it more about Acrobatics than—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: You could be the world's first axebeak surfer.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Acrobatics is really more about trying to stay on your feet. As you're falling, you could attempt some sort of tricky move.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: To do that.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah, that's good. I'll do the standard Animal Handling, but as I fall, I'll try to use the axebeak's head to swing myself back onto it.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Or just launched yourself forward.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Oh, can I do that? It's how far the axebeak gets, right, not how far—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Where you land on—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Where you land.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I'll kind of pull off its head. Yes, I will do that. Great idea.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Make an Animal Handling roll. All right, let's—yeah, let's—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: —see if my crazy streak continues. Come on, Animal Handling. Boo.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You get on, and this one is pretty wild. It bucks and immediately starts sprinting at a dead pace. You make it about forty feet—not bad, but there are at least ten rocks ahead of you—when something distracts it. It makes a sudden turn, and you can't keep it going straight. It starts running sideways across the field, and you decide this is your moment to get some distance. Make an Acrobatics check.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Can I do Acrobatics first to see if I can flip back onto it and stay on longer? I'd like another forty feet.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Sure, you can try. At the moment, you've lost control of it. It isn't running down the track; it's running toward the crowd. People stationed around the course are starting to grab the ropes, and everyone knows what to do. But you've lost control of the animal, so you aren't going to get any more distance from it.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I'll launch myself as far as I can. From here, it would take something pretty miraculous, but let's see what happens.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You think you're being tricky, trying to swing around its neck and launch yourself down the field for another five, ten, or maybe fifteen feet. But the axebeak makes another sudden turn, and you go flying five feet backward onto the ground. You're probably in about twentieth place. You did better than all the people whose stones are only ten feet out, but not particularly well.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I get up laughing at myself and at the moment—very cheerful about the whole thing.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Kenzo, not everyone's cut out to be an axebeak rider. I'm sure you'll find your mount, just like I found mine.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So,

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: This competition.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Um, you won.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: This competition, but I think the wager is for the overall results.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I think you win, right?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, well,

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: How did the other people—what place did Wellby ultimately come in?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So, ultimately—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Wellby, you've still got an archery competition coming up, I believe.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That's tomorrow. They do archery, and then horse archery.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: What's the pot for third, so I can give half of everything?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So it'd be seventy-five. Third is ten gold.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Wellby, you should see how you place in this other competition before you decide. You could win that one outright.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: No, the wager is about the axebeak riding and the quarterstaff competition.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Right, so take forty-eight of my gold.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Kenzo laughs. "Sometimes I talk shit, but sometimes I'm a monk. I don't care about the money."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Later, you watch the horseback-riding competition. During the axebeak competition, Havdar—one of the scouts—returned. He seems tired, although he's clearly ready to join the festivities.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Seeker, I can't wait to see your completed pictorial story.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Looking over my shoulder, you notice I'm writing, "I don't care about the money," drawing a little circle around it, and adding a little band from the circle to your mouth in the drawing. I'm like, "That could work. Speech balloon."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Havdar looks tired, almost as if he rode through the night. But he clearly isn't going to miss the riding competitions. He's well known and a bit haughty about his skill.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: We lost you there for a second.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Can you still hear me?

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Despite his exhaustion from hard travel, Havdar insists on competing. He's clearly masterful with a horse, and he's the type to work up the crowd and play up his skill. He performs tricks and show-off moves while riding, just to show up the competition a little. The day continues, and that evening there's a commotion as Alesh arrives after dinner. She recognizes you from your meeting on the road a few days ago. She looks exhausted and travel-stained, having clearly ridden farther and longer than Havdar. She pauses briefly to say hello.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: She says, "Of course, I think we have much to discuss. First, though, let me pass on my thanks—as I'm sure you've heard from many people—for everything you've done for Karawa. It really does mean the world to me. I cannot stay long. I must speak with Candrosa briefly, but I assume that, given your role in these events, you will be joining us for the council tomorrow."

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: She looks relieved. "We will speak soon." She rides off. You don't know what time the council will be tomorrow, but everyone is back now, so you expect a busy day.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: When you wake in the morning, a message from Candrosa is waiting for you: "Come. The village council will meet at ten o'clock. We would very much appreciate your wisdom and insight in these trying times." You know the council chamber—the place where you spoke with Kisa after returning. Let's take a short break here—five minutes.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Like five

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Five minutes or less.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Five minutes. Sounds good.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Where's your sister these days?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: In western Massachusetts. She's in the Pine Gap year.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Hmm.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Nantucket for a couple of years.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Oh, wow. No.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: A colleague told me the other day that there's a stereotype: Nantucket is the conservative island, and Martha's Vineyard is the liberal island.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I don't know. It wouldn't surprise me, though. Last year—or maybe this year—someone had a fundraiser three houses down from my parents. My dad was talking to the Secret Service guys last year.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Wow.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I think they organized a quick rally to hold up some signs.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Or your dad did? Yeah. Nice. Your parents spend a lot of time there versus New Hampshire? Wow, Tim looks severed from the waist up. This is really weird.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Your virtual background and chair interact in a strange way.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: It looked like you were severed from the waist up. Cool background.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Changing it to the village. Okay, everybody else set?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Yep.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You head to the village council chamber. The rest of the council has gathered. Candrosa nods in acknowledgment. Kisa smiles and greets each of you warmly, again offering her thanks. You also recognize Alesh and Havdar, the warrior-scout you saw in yesterday's riding competition. One additional person is unfamiliar to most of you: Suma, priestess of Jeevali. Delwath may have seen her around occasionally. She's a middle-aged woman with dark, curly hair and soft, friendly features. Though she doesn't recognize you, she may at least have heard of Delwath, and she greets you warmly.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Our saviors. Pleased to see you here. Peace be with the Five Siblings." Kisa urges everyone to sit around the circular table. Havdar stands first. He's a loud and brash young Dunmari, clearly skilled in both riding and battle. He bears his share of scars; apart from you, he seems the person in the room most likely to have seen combat. "I rode south and southeast, investigating the rumored attacks on the farms and orchards. I am saddened and upset to report that the rumors are true. In fact, the reality is far worse than any news that has reached us. Large bands of—"

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "—rampaging, hungry creatures, hyena-like in form but standing on two legs and fighting with weapons, have torn through our southern and southeastern farmlands. I expect a large column of refugees to arrive at Karawa within a day. Many fled as quickly as they could, but I fear many may also have died. Some of my men are protecting the retreat as best they can. I rode ahead to warn the town. I do not know what other news there is on the plains, but the best defense is a good offense. If we move quickly, find the hideout or base of whoever controls these creatures, and destroy it, we can defeat this threat." Horror and sadness cross the faces around the room. Candrosa nods along with Havdar. Alesh stands next. "I rode in a wide circuit east, north, and west, as far as the edge of the mountains.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "I rode fast and hard. I did not stop to talk or fight, but I can tell you that nothing is as it seems out on the plains.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "You may have heard rumors of storms that never end—rumors of upheaval and turmoil. I can tell you there is a storm of thunder, lightning, and wild wind sitting on the plains that does not seem to move. A stream of black water flows out of the mountains with the foul stench of blood. I also saw a small number of these creatures." Did I just cut out there?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: After the river that smelled like blood, there was something about the creatures.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The lightning storm, then the river that smelled like blood. Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: And then the river smells like blood, and then the creatures.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "I also saw these creatures—hyena-like, perhaps—who had skirted our eastern border and were probing north, looking for creatures to attack. I saw the remains of a sheep herd torn to pieces and eaten by a band of them, and I fled south. I do not have the answer, but I am not convinced our only danger lies to the south. We don't know the scope or true nature of this threat."

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "We need more than Havdar's war band. We need an army. We need the Samraat. This cannot simply be a matter of defending our borders; we must seek aid. I do not know the source of these problems, but while our immediate concern may be to the south, there is a greater danger here."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Quick question about Dunmari politics: is there a king? Who is the king of Dunmar, or—

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: So,

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Dunmar has a Samraat. Dunmar isn't highly organized: there isn't a structure of baronies and feudal lords. People tend to be independent, and the land is held in common. There isn't much private ownership across the plains. The Samraat's main power and responsibility is the ability to call a gathering—a greater council of Dunmari from around the kingdom—and, if that council decides, muster an army. The Samraat is far away and would—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well, the Samraat has a traveling court. They might spend time in Tokra or another city in winter. In summer, the court is almost certainly here or down on the coast.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Oh wow, traveling court.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That's fairly typical for most kingdoms like this.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Cool.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Chardon is different because it's organized in another way, but Dunmar's Samraat also travels. There are a few places that resemble capitals, but the Samraat is constantly moving. Dunmar has a strong divide between east and west, and southeastern Dunmar is almost completely independent. The Samraat's only significant influence there is the ability to lead an army. Kisa nods along with Alesh. "We cannot leave Karawa undefended, but I agree: this does not seem like something we can fight on our own." Havdar scoffs, confident he could fight it himself, but Alesh and Kisa don't share that confidence. Suma, the priestess, has been quiet through the discussion.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: She looks at both of them. "Havdar may be right. We may be able to defeat the threat to the south and find whoever—or whatever—is organizing and controlling this force, if there is some greater purpose or evil behind it. Alesh, yes, somebody must ride to the Samraat. But what we must do now is hard. People make the Dunmari, not places. We are used to traveling and living on the road. If we stay here, I fear many more will die. If Karawa is to survive as a people, if not a place, we must flee west—to Tokra or some defensible position where we can be safe until an army is organized and our borders are secure. If we can deal with the attackers, so much the better. But if we have to flee—"

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "—we should do so as soon as possible. Although nothing can be done without Jeevali's blessing, and no course will succeed until after the festival." Everyone is quiet for a moment. Candrosa looks to Kisa, and Kisa turns to you. "We have one voice to flee and one to attack the south and defend Karawa. We seem to be at an impasse. You have proved your worth before. What would you do? Will the council accept the wisdom of these strangers, who have already proven their dedication to our people through battle and danger?" Havdar scoffs, but everyone else nods. Seeing himself outnumbered, he says, "Fine. Let us hear what they have to say. I will accept their wisdom as well." Everyone looks expectantly at you.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I need a minute. I've been making notes and sketching the locations of the different forces on my map as we learn about them.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Music

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Oh, I'm not sharing my music. Sorry, I had good music for this.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Perhaps we should take a moment to confer as a group and return to the council.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Candrosa and Kisa look at each other for a moment. Kisa says, "I believe we would be interested in hearing your deliberations. Perhaps there is information we can share."

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Fair enough.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: —we haven't shared.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: We don't have anything to hide.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I don't know. Do you have anything to hide?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Don't think so.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Why don't we try to understand this situation more clearly?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: If the town flees to Tokra, how long would it take to pack up, move everyone, and organize the retreat?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Suma and Candrosa look at each other. Candrosa says, "Shakun will not leave our temple. But if the town is to flee, it could happen quickly—a few days after the festival, I believe." Kisa nods. Alesh adds, "Most people will be leaving within a day or two after the festival anyway. Most celebration and trading happens before then. I think we would need no more than three days after the festival for the town to empty, should that be our decision."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: But it also sounds like—oh, sorry. Go ahead, Wellby.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I think our danger isn't only—you've heard our stories of Raven's Hold, of some malevolent force extinguishing the light or doing some evil there. If the festival ends and your people scatter back to their fields and flocks, they'll be easy targets for anything coming from the south, north, or east. There may be more beyond what we destroyed. Until we know the threat is gone, it doesn't seem defensible to scatter again. We know the threat isn't only coming from the south. I don't see another course of action besides leaving.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Also, no matter what, the king must be found and an army raised.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Alesh nods. "Yes, Kenzo, I completely agree. I think that goes without saying. News of this must reach others. There is a larger danger at work here that we cannot defeat ourselves."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: If the safety of the town and its people is paramount, and this position cannot be defended, then if a retreat is necessary, so be it.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Then it begs the question: are Havdar's forces and our band sufficient to protect the retreat?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Havdar looks over the four of you. "I have forty men who will ride with me. How many do you have?"

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: You're looking at it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Are you experienced horse riders?"

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Next week,

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Now,

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Provide housing for horses.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well, that is not bad.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Alesh is pretty good, right, Delwath? Isn't she good at riding horses? Well, not your horse—the one we put in the barn.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You all know how to ride, but there's a difference between riding a horse and fighting effectively from horseback.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: No, we can't do that.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: What is the size of this evacuation—the total population?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Only about two hundred people live in the village. If everyone who would normally scatter across the plains stayed together and headed west, you'd be talking about a thousand people—maybe more. But those people have transportation and gear and are already planning to leave. In terms of organizing supplies, you're really talking about the two hundred people in town.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: A full evacuation seems like a vulnerable target. Among my people, we have the opposite impulse: under threat, we dig in. If the town is abandoned and overrun, do we lose something precious at its heart—the mysteries within the Temple of Shakun? Could the temple provide shelter? I've only been just inside the entrance, but if it could temporarily house many people, it might provide some defense. The impulse among my people points in that direction.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Candrosa sort of ponders for a moment.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Candrosa says, "We could perhaps shelter the village, if need be, though not everyone here for the festival. And let me reiterate: the Mystai of Shakun will not leave this village."

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Can they defend the temple alone?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: What resources do they have to defend it?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Candrosa looks around. "Fewer every day, it seems. But this is not a choice we can make. This temple has stood for many generations, and I will not be the one to leave it. If need be, we can seal the doors."

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I'll be right back, but don't wait on me. Wellby's just checked out for a minute.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: How long would it take this town to travel to Tokra?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "We would not be able to move fast. With all of us traveling, weeks, I would think."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: How long to find the king?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Alesh and Havdar look at each other, both about to speak. Alesh answers first. "It's a long ride. If I left right after the festival, hopefully no more than a few weeks—maybe several weeks, perhaps a month. I don't think we can count on support for several months, at least."

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: And these forces seen abroad—how soon might we expect an attack at our doors?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Havdar looks up. "I trust my men to do what they can. We are not easy to push around. But I don't know. We are protecting as many people fleeing north as we can—or at least that was the situation when I left, more than a day ago. It could be a few days or a week. I don't know these creatures' purpose. They did not seem to care for land, treasure, or food, and not all were traveling toward us. My scouts reported some bands heading east into the blasted plains and others heading south into the scorching desert where nobody lives or travels. I cannot honestly say whether they even intend to attack. If someone were after plunder or treasure, it would seem obvious. If someone were after chaos, perhaps they would wait until we left and attack us on the road. I don't know."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: What do you think?

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Your eyes are working

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: So, no idea. No idea.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: I think. Yeah.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: That was weird. I was saying stuff and wondering why everybody was ignoring me.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Sorry.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Did he say how many? How big is this force? Do we have a clear sense? He said he had forty people, right—forty men?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: He has forty people fighting for him.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I mean the hyena creatures. Do they number in the dozens or hundreds?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Dozens. There seem to be multiple small bands—some numbering in the dozens, some fewer—not all traveling in the same direction.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: It seems to me that some part of the town should flee—maybe all of it. But running ahead of the storm means we won't know what the storm is. A month could change the character of what is coming.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: In a month, the darkness at Raven's Hold could spread, and the storms could grow, all without us knowing what's there. It seems worth maintaining some forward base, even if the bulk of the people flee west.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Where's Raven's Hold on this map?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Candrosa says, "You've mentioned the darkness at Raven's Hold several times now. What is it that you refer to?"

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I'll briefly retell the council the story of the hobgoblin and the orb.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes, Wellby told Kisa. We can presume Kisa shared that information with the council.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Candrosa seems puzzled. "Something about Raven's Hold and the hyena creatures you fought in town seems similar. Do you think they might be connected?"

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: It's hard to know.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That ever-present hunger—unfilled, unquenchable hunger.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Also, what was the name of the man who turned to stone? Do any of you know Arcus? Alesh, we heard that you had interacted with him. There's some connection between the hobgoblin we killed and this halfling.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Alesh says, "Yes, I spoke to him."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Who is Arcus?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "He was interested in artifacts. He wanted to know—now that you mention it, he was asking about Raven's Hold. Wait, how do you know him?"

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I take out the drawing. "We found him in an unfortunately immobile state—completely turned to stone."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Alesh looks surprised. "That is unexpected. Now that you mention Raven's Hold, he was definitely asking about these ruins. He wanted to know about every Great War fort I could name. I mentioned one I've never visited because it's across the Great Gash, and Raven's Hold—an even larger, more impressive fort. It was one of our people's main strongholds before the Great War, and a great battle was fought there near the war's end. Many died. Seeker, you may be interested to know that I believe it contains some dwarven architecture."

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh, really?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Arcus was asking about every Great War fort, and he had a couple of items he said he'd found on the road. I never saw them; he said he gave them to the smith. They were also from the Great War era. He seemed very interested in the war's lost knowledge, though he never said why. Now that I think of it, I spent a lot of time talking while he listened. He hardly said a word through our entire conversation and just let me run on about history."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: What did you think of his character? What kind of man was he?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "He was interested in history. He wanted to hear what I had to say."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: We found him turned to stone at that fort across the Gash, where we slew the hobgoblin wizard—or sorcerer, or whatever he was—who was turning people to stone.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: A basilisk sorcerer.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Arcus was turned to stone, and we couldn't tell whether he was there to assist this evil creature or was simply searching in the wrong place at the wrong time. We couldn't discern his motivation.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "He didn't strike me as evil, but I'm not sure I can say I've ever met anybody who was. He seemed quiet, almost scholarly—quiet and curious. He was taking notes."

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I look down self-consciously at my notebook. "Scholarly people are often trustworthy."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Did we find a notebook?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Now,

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: While we're on the topic of artifacts, do you have that little horn on you? I'd like to see it.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah, I've got it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: He was carrying it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The coin was where he was found.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Right, right. Sorry.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You presume he was carrying it; it was on the ground. Alesh says, "Fascinating. What happens if you blow it?"

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: We haven't tried yet.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "That's a Dunmari motif. I think it dates from a little after the Great War."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "After the Great War, there was much chaos and destruction. Many scouts tried to keep our people safe and rode along the borders. I've found pieces of horns with a similar design. My amateur guess is that they were a symbol carried by scouts who protected the people—or perhaps that's projection, because that's what I do and the horns look impressive. I don't really know, but I'd be curious to learn what happens if you blow it."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: We'll try that experiment another time.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: There were some people in town who suggested travelers have been coming through all winter.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Yes, there have been a few. None seemed as interested in history as Arcus, but they were passing east, and I don't know whether any returned. That's rather odd, now that you mention it."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: There's a fort to the southeast. What's that fort?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: On the map? That's very far southeast. What's its name?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: We haven't talked about yet.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That's more than a week's travel. That's near where Delwath appeared. This area here is—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: —where many farms and irrigation works are, where dates grow, in the eastern shadow of the mesa. Karawa is on the other side. This is what people mean when they talk about the southeast, not that fort—although you never really know.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Kharsan, yeah. What's that city south of Tokra—the other big walled city?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It's another Dunmari city. You would know what it's called. Where's my—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Money doesn't matter.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Doesn't matter. It's another Dunmari city: Kharsan.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: In any scenario where we defend Karawa—whether only the priests remain or a larger group stays—it's worth considering that I can rapidly raise simple earthworks. I could build a bulwark around the temple or perhaps a larger low wall. I can magically manipulate earth to do that, if needed.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: How much protection does Tokra offer?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Tokra offers people and warriors—not so much the city's protection as safety in numbers. If there are only several dozen of these creatures, then a hundred, perhaps fewer, skilled soldiers might be all that's necessary."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: For the townspeople, it feels like there are only two options: stay here or go to Tokra. Maybe I'm misunderstanding, but those are the two primary options. Is that right?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Kisa says, "Yes, indeed. Those seem to be our two options. The question is: do we stay and organize a defense, do we flee, or do we ride out to attack? Not the townspeople, obviously."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "We have Havdar and his forty riders, and little else. Perhaps a few dozen more soldiers can be scraped together from the men and women in town for the festival—perhaps twenty or thirty. We can certainly muster a defense.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "But what are we defending against? Is it this one attack, evil magic, floods, lightning, plague? For how long do we need to stay?"

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Yeah, it just—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: It feels like there's danger in traveling to Tokra. If the village moves, it will probably take all of Havdar's men and us to protect the villagers safely, because the threat is unknown. If we stay and send even a small force to investigate, that similarly weakens our defense against the unknown.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: It seems to me that a mounted group moving west could travel relatively quickly. Are there enough mounts for the whole village?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "That should be possible. Supplies are the greater challenge."

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: If the village stays, are stores already laid in, or would we need to accumulate them?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "We have animals and preserved food, yes. Transporting it all, should we flee, is the challenge."

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: But the village could potentially be self-sufficient under siege for several weeks?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: And it has its own water supply. Yes, of course.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: How secure can the temple be made?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I'm

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I'm sure Shakun has some expertise in this area.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Candrosa looks around. "These words do not leave this room. A month ago, I would have said it was entirely impenetrable. Today, I don't know."

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: What has changed?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "My faith in Shakun's power—or my ability to access Shakun's power."

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: When was the last time you heard Shakun's voice?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "That is difficult to answer, because Shakun does not always speak in a clear voice. But—"

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "—it has been many months since I was fully confident she was with us, and many weeks since I was fully confident our defenses would hold."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Here's a proposal. The safest place for the villagers is ultimately Tokra. The journey is dangerous, but two hundred Dunmari on horseback—skilled riders—will find greater safety if they can reach the city. No matter what, Alesh needs to find the Samraat and raise an army. The question is—what's the scout's name again?

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Havdar.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: The great unknown—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: —is what these forces are and what danger they pose. We still don't know. If the village can be routed to Tokra, and Havdar's men can protect the villagers, then our group could investigate further. Even when the army is raised, whether everyone is in Tokra or here in Karawa, we'll be at a disadvantage if we don't understand this danger. The four of us are fast, nimble, and stealthy. We can learn as much as possible, then return with information to Tokra or Karawa—whichever offers the better defense. Tokra seems safest, if the village can reach it quickly enough.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: And if Havdar's men are sufficient to protect them during the journey, that's one possibility.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I think that's the right move. I hope Havdar can return east if there are enough soldiers to hold Tokra. Once the village is evacuated, he could come back to defend the temple and continue scouting from here as a base—what becomes a military outpost.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: But one with a very important temple.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: But holding it seems valuable for now.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: The closest

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: It's the closest outpost to these strange events. But I think Wellby is right: the village can only be held as a fortress.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: So the villagers should move to Tokra, then?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: That would be my thinking. Yes.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: It's worth noting that when we explored the crumbling fort to the east, we found and destroyed something that immediately eliminated much of the danger here. If we find another crumbling fort, we may eliminate more danger. How many of these forts are there? If we go to the fort north of here, we might reduce some danger—but where else is it coming from?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Havdar perks up. "This man speaks sense. My men could certainly protect a column of Dunmari fleeing west. I could probably double my force by mustering people here for the festival; there are riders and fighters among them. But where do we attack? We cannot simply run and give no thought to striking back or protecting this land—our home. Do we go south, where most of the hyena creatures seem to be and where the greatest danger appears to lie? That's where I would ride. Or do we go north, where it seems—"

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "—well, to be honest, it seems like there's horrible magic up there. That would not be my first choice."

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Is there an abandoned fort to the south?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: There are several. The big city Delwath appeared near is also in that direction. Perhaps nothing is as large or notable as Raven's Hold, but Alesh can sketch the locations of the significant southern ruins on a map.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: South or north, though?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I roll my map out on the table and use Minor Illusion to make animated figures representing us, the town, a column fleeing it, defenders around it, the endless lightning storm, and the stream of blood. I've spent the last few minutes making it all appear as glowing, illusory figures above the table.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Awesome. Havdar looks impressed.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: That was an angle.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: And

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Havdar, I think you're better suited to meet roving bands of gnoll people in the field, while we're better suited to investigate ancient magic. I look at the other three. I mean, I'm not suited to the ancient-magic part, but hopefully—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: He is an axebeak rider. Maybe you're suited to meet some creatures in the hills.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Yeah, as long as they're within 75 feet.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: My thought is that we don't understand the dangers, and confronting them head-on may be deadly even for us. Our mission should be reconnaissance: understand the threat's true scope, then return with information to Candrosa and the Mystai if Karawa remains an outpost. Havdar, if your band first escorts the villagers west to Tokra, you can return to help Candrosa fortify Karawa while we investigate north or south. We can rally here after our investigation and decide whether to attack. Meanwhile, Alesh can work to rally the king's troops. After reconnaissance, we can make a better plan to attack or defend, depending on what we're facing.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Havdar looks around the room. "I said I would agree to your wisdom, and I stand by that. But I feel we can fight this. I can rally more troops. I'm sure I can find people in the village—people here for the festival—who will fight, perhaps enough both to guard those who flee and to attack. South or north, I will go where you direct me."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: We don't doubt the strength of your men. But this conversation has made clear that we don't understand what we're up against—what may lie north or south. Our first priority must be protecting the townspeople. You will have an opportunity to demonstrate your strength in battle, but we should fight after we understand the threat.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Havdar says, "As I said, I will follow your wisdom. Better not to win a battle only to lose the war."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I glance around, first at our group and then at everyone. "What do you all think?"

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I think Kenzo speaks with wisdom. Information will be necessary to fight these battles. Behind the dozen hyenas you've seen, there could be a thousand more.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I advise preparing the evacuation and a contingency plan to shelter inside the temple indefinitely if the evacuation must be abandoned or people have to return.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: We don't know when an attack could strike.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: We should fortify the temple no matter what. If it will become a fortress—even just for Candrosa and the Mystai—we should begin while the festival winds down. We can prepare the villagers to evacuate west and, before we leave north or south, have the temple well fortified for Candrosa and for Havdar and any troops who return.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Havdar, if you can muster enough soldiers to split your forces—enough to defend those fleeing west and strike out at the same time—so much the better.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Bringing us south before you go—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: South or north?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I think striking south is premature, based on the reports we've heard.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: So far,

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: There's no commander and no plan that we can see. We don't know what they're doing.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Havdar says, "They seem hell-bent on destruction and chaos—killing and eating anything in their path. I've seen these creatures."

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Hunger, that can't be filled.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Maybe

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: The danger isn't that—

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: —you die gloriously in battle. The danger is that you and your men return to Karawa as these hyena creatures and kill your friends and family.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Havdar looks shaken, as if he had not considered that possibility. "Perhaps you do speak wisdom."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: You and your men will be of greatest service protecting the townspeople and their families. As Candrosa and Kisa said, Karawa is not this place; Karawa is its people. The people need the greatest protection, and I don't think even dividing your force is wise. Maintain your entire force and ensure that the town can resettle safely over the next few weeks. Afterward, rally back here to Karawa. In the meantime, we'll learn as much as we can. Then we can devise the best strategy for attack, knowing the Samraat's army is also being raised.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I can do that.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I glance around at Candrosa, Kisa—everyone.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: "What are your thoughts on this plan? This is not the time to carry doubts or regrets. Please speak your minds."

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I'm making an animated version of the Kenzo plan.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Suma, the priestess of Jeevali, has been quiet. She speaks. "Karawa is its people. We know how to run. We know how to ride.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Candrosa, I know you will not leave this place. But I truly think our people can escape. Havdar, if you can protect us to Tokra, then ride to glory however you wish afterward. That will keep the most people alive." Kisa nods as Suma speaks. "I know we must protect the temple. It was here before the town and cannot be abandoned, Candrosa, and I am not asking you to do that. But I think Kenzo's plan for the people to flee is right. If we warn everyone at the festival, word will spread. People can cross the plains and warn those who have not returned to town: head west of the river. If everyone heads west, fewer people will die."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: As you will soon appreciate, Seeker has great protective powers and can help fortify the temple. We will benefit greatly from the dwarf's help in protecting Candrosa and the Mystai.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: We'll see. I only have what I have to work with.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: As you have this three-dimensional interface floating in front of us.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Havdar says, "I will muster who I can, raise what force I can, and protect those fleeing west—perhaps leaving a small guard to support Candrosa. Then I will return and gather again in Karawa before we attack."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: What do you think, Oh, sorry. Good.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Suma says, "I will lead the evacuation with Kisa. We can make sure as many people head west as possible, while Alesh rides as fast as she can for the king."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Candrosa, what do you think of this plan?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Candrosa says, "I trust in your experience and wisdom. For all my time in Karawa, and whatever skill I possess, I have never been east of our border. I have never crossed the blasted plains or the Great Gash. You have, and you have seen what is out there. As Delwath said, the danger of attacking may be greater and more terrible than merely a glorious death in battle. The only way to keep as many people alive as possible is to flee until we know what we're facing. Even without our magic, the temple can be fortified. It is stone and solid. We have water and food.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "If we have to ask Seeker to seal the doors so nothing can come or go, then we will survive until you return."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: The only question remaining for us is: where do we go?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Do we go north or south?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I need you to decide, because—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yeah, you've got to prepare.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: North. Yes.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I agree.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Why north?

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: North

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Why north? The threat seems to be coming from there.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: We have a lead. We know there was a sorcerer or wizard there—some magic. It's a definite location where someone created this effect, though there may be many other strange threats.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: If we can find such a thing—

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: It seems almost tangible.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Before we depart, I think we should make a concerted effort to reach Shakun. We may fail, but it's worth participating in the attempt.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Um,

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Let's see.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: We should bring the spear tips.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Agreed. It's not my place to say this, but we talked about not wanting to abandon the temple. It's possible the temple has already been abandoned—that Shakun has already abandoned it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Candrosa says, "I cannot deny that. But there is more to the temple than Shakun's presence. There is our history as well, and that I will not leave behind."

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: And whatever I saw with Stone Sense—which I don't remember—some cache of valuables.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You couldn't quite determine what it was, but it was clearly something unusual that you had never encountered before—and extremely valuable.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: And deep inside

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And deep inside just at the edge of the range of your sense

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I think this plan is sound. My only concern is—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: —we will not understand the dangers of the south. Our knowledge of the threat will be incomplete.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: The other thing we could do—Havdar, after your full force ensures the people's safety, if we reconvene here after investigating the north, we could discuss how to investigate the south. Ideally, we would do both simultaneously, but I don't know if there's a good way to do that.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You mean scout south and north at the same time?

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: A small party could scout south.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Havdar, do you have a small group of men you trust? Reconnaissance only—no engagement.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Alesh looks at Havdar.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I know this kind of—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: At this point, he's probably been dead for fifty years.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Alesh says, "Havdar, this is what I do. Perhaps you—or someone else we trust—could meet with the king and request aid and a muster. I could join a few of your quieter, faster riders and investigate the south myself."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Are there politics involved in approaching the king? Does the emissary matter?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Kisa snorts. "There's always politics. The king doesn't care about us. Yes, of course the emissary matters."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Who's the best emissary? Is it Alesh?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Kisa says, "I trust Alesh. But as the best emissary? Perhaps we can think of someone else who can get the king's attention. Those who live in the cushy wetlands to the west forget about us and our traditions. To them, Chardon is where the money is; Chardon is the future. I'm not so sure. But you raise a good point. Alesh, perhaps we can confer. If you're going to scout—which I understand is what you do—we may be able to propose another emissary. You can ride fast, but perhaps someone else can get the job done."

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I'll defer to you on the politics; you know them better than we do. If we understand the king's relationships and what might bend the Samraat's ear in our favor, send the best emissary and allow the other best riders to head south—again, reconnaissance and investigation only. When we reconvene in Karawa, hopefully in several weeks, we'll have the information we need to—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Make the next—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: —make the next plan.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Agreed.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I look around at everybody.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Everybody sort of nods.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Are we decided?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Kisa says, "We are decided. The morning after the festival, we will begin organizing the retreat."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "I suggest you leave on your respective missions as soon as possible after the festival. If there is anything we can do or provide to speed you on your way, let us know." She directs that to you, Alesh, and Havdar—everyone other than Kisa, Suma, and Candrosa. With that, I think we've reached a good place to call it a night.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Yep.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Word.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Bass
